text.p: These are some of the leading stories in Israeli newspapers on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
GLOBES

- No evidence found against Prime Minister Netanyahu in investigation into allegations of corruption in short-lived apppointment of attorney general in January; investigation continues against other figures in affair.
- Bezeq appoints acting director general.

- Netanyahu says third group interested in acquiring Bank Hapoalim; doesn't say who; Globes says it's known that, in addition to two known bidders two others have taken out forms but only first two groups are thought serious.
HAARETZ
- Night cabinet meeting on further redeployment in West Bank.
- Senior legal source: Charges in attorney general affair will be minor.
- Infrastructure Minister Sharon renewing drive to build along Israel's pre-1967 war border.
- U.S. air force ordered U.S. companies working in Saudi Arabia not to employ Jews.
JERUSALEM POST
- Cabinet debates West Bank pullback of up to 10 percent.
- U.S. Navy to aid in search for Israeli submarine lost in 1960s.
- U.S. Reform Jewish movement links with Marranos, Jews long ago forced to convert in Spain who kept up Jewish practise secretly.
- Palestinian Authority calls for march against Israel building East Jerusalem Jewish settlement.
- Insurance heads convicted of price fixing could face dismissal.
YEDIOTH AHRONOTH
- Harsh debate on further withdrawal.
- U.S. ambasssador to Israel, ultra-rightwing MP exchange insults at dedication of centre named after Yitzhak Rabin.
- Foreign Minister Levy considers delaying visit to U.S. due to atmosphere over decision to build Jewish settlement in Arab East Jerusalem.
MAARIV
- Tense debate on next West Bank withdrawal.
- U.S. ambassador called Netanyahu and told him U.S. expected significant pullback.
- Syria says there will not be peace under Netanyahu.
- PLO police save two Israeli soldiers in Gaza; soldiers had lost their way and were attacked by crowd.
